title: Record companies, big signing money, and musicians who went commercial
summary: Sam argues companies push musicians into commercial music, naming Dexter Gordon, Sonny Rollins, Donald Byrd and Miles.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Um, um, well I can't see where you got to put--I get back to ah, what I was saying. I wrote music man, see--this music-the black man's music I'm speaking of-now, you see, those guys are playing the white man's music because the white man is making--he's the man that's making the money, you see? He's sitting in his lavishly apart--um, um office on Park Avenue, you know, uh, Hollywood Boulevard in California, or somewhere else, some big office in London or somewhere uh, with his Rolls Royce and chauffeur downstairs waiting for him and he's, and they give these guys, say like uh, you know, a few bucks, you know, just that's the most money they have heard from or seen in their life and jump at it. And they say, OK, we want you to play the same the same kind of music; we want you to play this type of

music. This is not the music that you want to play, but you are ordered to play that. It's the same as therefore when Columbia starts signing, you know, all the musicians if you remember when all this kind of--this is not, uh, their choice, you know? Sure, he hand them out about ten grand, here we just want you to sign--$10,000, $10,000, $10,000, $10,000--we want you to sign. At one time when I saw these guys that are--that have never seen $10,000 all at once in their life, yeah, you know, you jump at it. And then you go to the studio to, to record and and and, this man tells you, "I want you to record this music this way because this is what we are selling; we are selling. This is what we are pushing, don't bring none of that, none of your music in here." Dexter Gordon refused to play that music. What did they do? Kicked Dexter--kicked Dexter Gordon out. Jimmy Heath I've, I've seen him make his change over. Maybe that's what they need, you know, just, to stay out there, just so that their band can survive, you see? OK. If you notice I can go on and start calling musicians--there's the great Sonny Rollins; which was my favorite for years man. But I can't stand him now, man, I wouldn't even--I wouldn't have any of that stuff down, you know, on, on my machine, you know. He's gone over. You've got your great Donald Byrd, the Black Byrds. And if you tell me that the music that Donald Byrd is playing is jazz music--then, man, I might as well get out of the business, you know.

Miles Davis. Well his stuff was a little confused a little bit, you know. On, on a more of a freedom style--rock. But all of it, man, it's nothing but the so called, the uh, young people music, man, you know. It, it it which don't have nothing to do with the black man's classic music. It don't have a thing to do with it. Nothing to do with it.
